    args = [sys.executable, "-m", "mlx_lm", "server", "--model", config.MODEL,
            "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", config.PORT]
    if config.has_adapter():
        args += ["--adapter-path", config.ADAPTERS]
        print(f"adapter: {config.active_version()}")
    else:
        print("(no adapter yet — serving base model; run train first for footprint behavior)")
    print(f"OpenAI-compatible API: http://127.0.0.1:{config.PORT}/v1  (model name: footprint)")
    subprocess.run(args, check=True)
def serve():
    import torch
    from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(config.MODEL)
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(config.MODEL, torch_dtype="auto", device_map="auto")
    if config.has_adapter():
        from peft import PeftModel
        model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(model, config.ADAPTERS)
    else:
        print("(no adapter yet — serving base model; run train first for footprint behavior)")
    model.eval()

    def generate(messages, max_tokens, temperature):
        ids = tok.apply_chat_template(messages, add_generation_prompt=True,
                                      return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            out = model.generate(ids, max_new_tokens=max_tokens, do_sample=temperature > 0,
                                 temperature=max(temperature, 1e-3),
                                 pad_token_id=tok.eos_token_id)
        return tok.decode(out[0][ids.shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True)

    class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def _json(self, obj, ctype="application/json"):
            body = json.dumps(obj).encode()
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", ctype)
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)

        def do_GET(self):
            if self.path.startswith("/v1/models"):
                self._json({"object": "list", "data": [{"id": "footprint", "object": "model"}]})
            else:
                self.send_error(404)

        def do_POST(self):
            if self.path.rstrip("/") != "/v1/chat/completions":
                self.send_error(404)
                return
            req = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
            text = generate(req.get("messages", []), req.get("max_tokens") or 1024,
                            req.get("temperature") if req.get("temperature") is not None else 0.7)
            if req.get("stream"):
                # ponytail: whole answer as one SSE chunk; true token streaming if UX needs it
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
                self.end_headers()
                for payload in (
                        {"id": "fp", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "model": "footprint",
                         "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": text},
                                      "finish_reason": None}]},
                        {"id": "fp", "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "model": "footprint",
                         "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}):
                    self.wfile.write(f"data: {json.dumps(payload)}\n\n".encode())
                self.wfile.write(b"data: [DONE]\n\n")
            else:
                self._json({"id": "fp", "object": "chat.completion", "model": "footprint",
                            "choices": [{"index": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": text},
                                         "finish_reason": "stop"}]})

        def log_message(self, *a):
            pass

    print(f"OpenAI-compatible API: http://127.0.0.1:{config.PORT}/v1  (model name: footprint)\n"
          f"device: {'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'}")
    ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", int(config.PORT)), Handler).serve_forever()
def _opencode():
    cfg_path = os.path.join(config.OPENCODE, "opencode.json")
    cfg = json.load(open(cfg_path, encoding="utf-8")) if os.path.exists(cfg_path) else {"$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json"}
    cfg.setdefault("provider", {})["footprint"] = {
        "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible", "name": "footprint",
        "options": {"baseURL": f"http://127.0.0.1:{config.PORT}/v1"},
        "models": {"footprint": {"name": "footprint"}}}
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(config.OPENCODE, "commands"), exist_ok=True)
    with open(cfg_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(cfg, f, indent=2)
    with open(os.path.join(config.OPENCODE, "commands", "footprint.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("---\ndescription: do task with footprint — local model trained on your Claude sessions\n"
                "model: footprint/footprint\n---\n$ARGUMENTS\n")


def install():
    """Register the server with the OS so it runs itself. User never runs serve."""
    if not os.path.exists(config.VENV_PY):
        sys.exit("no .venv. run: footprint setup")
    if config.IS_MAC:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(config.LAUNCHD), exist_ok=True)
        with open(config.LAUNCHD, "wb") as f:
            plistlib.dump({"Label": "com.footprint.serve",
                           "ProgramArguments": [config.VENV_PY, config.ENTRY, "serve"],
                           "RunAtLoad": True, "KeepAlive": True,
                           "StandardOutPath": "/tmp/footprint-serve.log",
                           "StandardErrorPath": "/tmp/footprint-serve.log"}, f)
        subprocess.run(["launchctl", "unload", config.LAUNCHD], capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(["launchctl", "load", "-w", config.LAUNCHD], check=True)
        how = "launchd (log: /tmp/footprint-serve.log)"
    elif config.IS_WIN:
        subprocess.run(["schtasks", "/Create", "/F", "/TN", "footprint-serve", "/SC", "ONLOGON",
                        "/TR", f'"{config.VENV_PY}" "{config.ENTRY}" serve'], check=True)
        subprocess.run(["schtasks", "/Run", "/TN", "footprint-serve"], check=True)
        how = "Task Scheduler (task: footprint-serve)"
    else:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(config.SYSTEMD), exist_ok=True)
        with open(config.SYSTEMD, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("[Unit]\nDescription=footprint local model server\n\n"
                    f"[Service]\nExecStart={config.VENV_PY} {config.ENTRY} serve\nRestart=always\n\n"
                    "[Install]\nWantedBy=default.target\n")
        subprocess.run(["systemctl", "--user", "daemon-reload"], check=True)
        subprocess.run(["systemctl", "--user", "enable", "--now", "footprint"], check=True)
        how = "systemd --user (journalctl --user -u footprint)"
    _opencode()
    print(f"installed:\n"
          f"  server: {how} keeps http://127.0.0.1:{config.PORT}/v1 running\n"
          f"  opencode: /footprint <task> uses it; or pick model 'footprint' via /models\n"
          f"  cursor/codex: base URL http://127.0.0.1:{config.PORT}/v1, any api key")

content.text:
footprint serves a local OpenAI-compatible API at `http://127.0.0.1:8399/v1`, but on Mac it is probably serving the base Qwen model without your LoRA. I found two bugs in mlx_lm 0.31.3 (the version in `.venv`) that break the Mac path. I only tested them with the model load stubbed out; I haven't seen them hit a real server, and nothing is installed or running on your machine right now.

**How each OS serves:**
- **Mac:** `mlx_backend.serve()` (`footprint_core/backends/mlx_backend.py:249`) starts mlx_lm's own server, `mlx_lm server --model <Qwen> --adapter-path adapters/`.
- **Linux / Windows:** `torch_backend.serve()` is our own small HTTP server, using transformers + peft with the adapter on top. It only handles `/v1/models` and `/v1/chat/completions`, and streaming sends the whole answer as one chunk.
- **Running it:** `footprint install` (`service.py:64`) registers launchd on Mac, systemd on Linux, or Task Scheduler on Windows, so it starts at login and restarts on crash. It also writes the OpenCode provider `footprint/footprint` and the `/footprint` command.

**The two bugs:**
1. **The adapter is dropped.** In `ModelProvider.load()`, mlx_lm maps `default_model` to the base model path first, then looks up the adapter under that new key, finds nothing, and loads with no adapter. My test recorded `('BASE', None, None)` even with `--adapter-path` set. So the base model would answer, and the fine-tuning would have no effect.
2. **The model name `footprint` breaks Mac requests.** OpenCode and Cursor send `"model": "footprint"`. mlx_lm treats that as a Hugging Face repo name and tries to load it, which fails, or fails offline.

The torch path doesn't have either problem.

**Fix options:**
- **(a) Fuse at train time (smallest):** after the test gate passes, run `mlx_lm fuse` to merge the adapter into one model folder, then serve that folder. This fixes bug 1. For bug 2, we'd also need to map the name `footprint` to that folder, either with a small wrapper around the server or by changing the OpenCode model id.
- **(b) Serve through Ollama** (the earlier suggestion): it loads the adapter from a Modelfile and serves under whatever name we choose, so both bugs go away. It needs the adapter converted to GGUF, and it's the bigger change.

I'd do (a) now and leave (b) for later. Want me to make that fix?

content.text:
Ollama would barely reduce CPU on your Mac, but it would cut it a lot on Linux and Windows.

**Mac (your machine):** no real CPU saving. MLX and Ollama both run the model on the Apple GPU through Metal, so the CPU stays mostly idle while text is generated. On Apple Silicon, MLX is usually as fast as Ollama or faster.

**Idle memory on Mac:** Ollama does help here. It unloads the model after 5 idle minutes by default (`keep_alive`), which frees about 1–2 GB of RAM. The catch is a delay of a few seconds on the next request while it loads again. `mlx_lm server` keeps the model loaded the whole time, but uses close to 0% CPU while idle.

**Linux / Windows without a GPU:** big win. Our torch server runs the full-precision model on the CPU, which is slow and keeps the cores busy. import glob, hashlib, json, os, shutil, sys, time

from . import config

    return sorted((os.path.basename(d) for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, "v*"))
                   if os.path.basename(d)[1:].isdigit()), key=lambda v: int(v[1:]))


def metrics(v):

def new_version():

    vs = versions()
    v = f"v{int(vs[-1][1:]) + 1 if vs else 1}"
    path = os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, v)

def start(sig):
    """Where a training run goes. An unfinished newest version (no metrics.json) with the same data + LoRA
    settings is resumed -> (v, path, progress). Unfinished with other settings is wiped and reused (its
    checkpoints can't load under a different LoRA shape). Otherwise a fresh version -> (v, path, None)."""
    migrate()
    vs = versions()
    last = vs[-1] if vs else None
    if last and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, last, "metrics.json")) \
            and last != config.active_version():
        path = os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, last)
        try:
            prog = json.load(open(os.path.join(path, "progress.json"), encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            prog = {}
        if prog.get("sig") == sig and 0 < prog.get("done", 0) < prog.get("iters", 0):
            return last, path, prog
        print(f"discarding unfinished {last} (stopped before any checkpoint, or data/settings changed since)")
        shutil.rmtree(path)
        os.makedirs(path)
        return last, path, None
    v, path = new_version()
    return v, path, None


def save_progress(path, prog):
    tmp = os.path.join(path, "progress.json.tmp")
    json.dump(prog, open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8"), indent=1)
    os.replace(tmp, os.path.join(path, "progress.json"))


def data_hash():
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for name in ("train", "valid", "test"):
        p = os.path.join(config.DATA, f"{name}.jsonl")
        if os.path.exists(p):

    return h.hexdigest()[:12]


def finish(v, m):

    m = {"version": v, "model": config.MODEL, "data": data_hash(), "created": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), **m}
    json.dump(m, open(os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, v, "metrics.json"), "w"), indent=1)

    old = metrics(cur).get("test_loss") if cur else None

    else:

def use(v, quiet=False):

    open(os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, "active"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write(v)

    cur = config.active_version()
    print(f"adapters for {config.MODEL}:")
    for v in versions():
        m = metrics(v)
        print(f"  {'*' if v == cur else ' '} {v}  {m.get('format', ''):<22} test loss {m.get('test_loss', '?')}  "
              f"val {m.get('val_loss', '?')}  best iter {m.get('best_iter', '?')}  data {m.get('data', '?')}  {m.get('created', '')}")
    if not versions():
        print("  none yet. run: footprint collect && footprint train")


if __name__ == "__main__":  # self-check: versions, gate, migrate, rollback in a temp root
    import tempfile
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    config.ADAPTER_ROOT, config.DATA = d, d
    config.MODEL_ADAPTERS = os.path.join(d, "m")
    open(os.path.join(d, "adapters.safetensors"), "w").write("old")

def new_version():
    migrate()
    vs = versions()
    v = f"v{int(vs[-1][1:]) + 1 if vs else 1}"
    path = os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, v)
    os.makedirs(path)
    return v, path


def start(sig):
    """Where a training run goes. An unfinished newest version (no metrics.json) with the same data + LoRA
    settings is resumed -> (v, path, progress). Unfinished with other settings is wiped and reused (its
    checkpoints can't load under a different LoRA shape). Otherwise a fresh version -> (v, path, None)."""
    migrate()
    vs = versions()
    last = vs[-1] if vs else None
    if last and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, last, "metrics.json")) \
            and last != config.active_version():
        path = os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, last)
        try:
            prog = json.load(open(os.path.join(path, "progress.json"), encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            prog = {}
        if prog.get("sig") == sig and 0 < prog.get("done", 0) < prog.get("iters", 0):
            return last, path, prog
        print(f"discarding unfinished {last} (stopped before any checkpoint, or data/settings changed since)")
        shutil.rmtree(path)
        os.makedirs(path)
        return last, path, None
    v, path = new_version()
    return v, path, None


def save_progress(path, prog):
    tmp = os.path.join(path, "progress.json.tmp")
    json.dump(prog, open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8"), indent=1)
    os.replace(tmp, os.path.join(path, "progress.json"))


def data_hash():
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for name in ("train", "valid", "test"):
        p = os.path.join(config.DATA, f"{name}.jsonl")
        if os.path.exists(p):
            h.update(open(p, "rb").read())
    return h.hexdigest()[:12]


def finish(v, m):
    """Save metrics; go live only if no adapter is active or this one has a lower test loss."""
    m = {"version": v, "model": config.MODEL, "data": data_hash(), "created": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), **m}
    json.dump(m, open(os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, v, "metrics.json"), "w"), indent=1)
    cur = config.active_version()
    old = metrics(cur).get("test_loss") if cur else None
    if cur is None or (m.get("test_loss") is not None and (old is None or m["test_loss"] < old)):
        use(v, quiet=True)
        print(f"{v} is now active (test loss {m.get('test_loss')} vs {old if cur else 'none'}). "
              f"Gate it: footprint bench run <footprint model in opencode> --memory=both; rollback: footprint adapter use {cur}"
              if cur else f"{v} is now active.")
    else:
        print(f"{v} saved but NOT active: test loss {m.get('test_loss')} is not better than {cur}'s {old}. "
              f"Use anyway: footprint adapter use {v}")


def use(v, quiet=False):
    if v not in versions():
        sys.exit(f"no {v}. have: {', '.join(versions()) or 'none'}")
    open(os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, "active"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write(v)
    if not quiet:
        print(f"active adapter: {v} — restart the server to load it (footprint serve, or re-run footprint install)")


def main(argv=()):
    migrate()
    if argv[:1] == ["use"] and len(argv) > 1:
        return use(argv[1])
    cur = config.active_version()
    print(f"adapters for {config.MODEL}:")
    for v in versions():
        m = metrics(v)
        print(f"  {'*' if v == cur else ' '} {v}  {m.get('format', ''):<22} test loss {m.get('test_loss', '?')}  "
              f"val {m.get('val_loss', '?')}  best iter {m.get('best_iter', '?')}  data {m.get('data', '?')}  {m.get('created', '')}")
    if not versions():
        print("  none yet. run: footprint collect && footprint train")


if __name__ == "__main__":  # self-check: versions, gate, migrate, rollback in a temp root
    import tempfile
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    config.ADAPTER_ROOT, config.DATA = d, d
    config.MODEL_ADAPTERS = os.path.join(d, "m")
    open(os.path.join(d, "adapters.safetensors"), "w").write("old")
    v, p = new_version()  # migrates legacy to v1 (active), returns v2
    assert v == "v2" and versions() == ["v1", "v2"] and config.active_version() == "v1", (v, versions())
    finish("v2", {"test_loss": 2.0, "format": "native-v2"})
    assert config.active_version() == "v2"  # legacy had no test loss: v2 wins
    v3, _ = new_version()
    finish(v3, {"test_loss": 2.5})
    assert config.active_version() == "v2"  # worse: saved, not live

"""Serve through Ollama: LoRA adapter -> GGUF adapter -> `ollama create footprint` on Ollama's own base.

  adapters/<model>/vN/adapters.safetensors (MLX)  or  adapter_model.safetensors (PEFT, torch backend)
    -> vN/adapter.gguf  (a few MB; llama.cpp LoRA format)
    -> Modelfile: FROM <ollama base>  ADAPTER vN/adapter.gguf
    -> model "footprint" at http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1  (Ollama runs itself: app / brew service / systemd)
"""
import json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, urllib.request

from . import config

URL = os.environ.get("OLLAMA_HOST", "http://127.0.0.1:11434").rstrip("/")
if "://" not in URL:
    URL = "http://" + URL
NAME = "footprint"
# HF layer names -> llama.cpp/GGUF names (Qwen2 / Llama-style blocks)
PROJ = {"self_attn.q_proj": "attn_q", "self_attn.k_proj": "attn_k", "self_attn.v_proj": "attn_v",
        "self_attn.o_proj": "attn_output", "mlp.gate_proj": "ffn_gate", "mlp.up_proj": "ffn_up",
        "mlp.down_proj": "ffn_down"}


def base():
    """Ollama tag of the same base model footprint trained on."""
    if os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_OLLAMA_BASE"):
        return os.environ["FOOTPRINT_OLLAMA_BASE"]
    m = re.search(r"Qwen2\.5-Coder-([\d.]+)B", config.MODEL, re.I)
    if not m:
        sys.exit(f"no Ollama base known for {config.MODEL}. set FOOTPRINT_OLLAMA_BASE (e.g. qwen2.5-coder:7b)")
    return f"qwen2.5-coder:{m.group(1)}b"


def _lora(path):
    """-> ({(layer, proj): (A[r,in], B[out,r])}, alpha) from an MLX or PEFT adapter dir."""
    from safetensors.numpy import load_file
    cfg = json.load(open(os.path.join(path, "adapter_config.json"), encoding="utf-8"))
    pairs = {}
    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(path, "adapter_model.safetensors")):  # PEFT: lora_A.weight [r,in], lora_B.weight [out,r]
        for k, t in load_file(os.path.join(path, "adapter_model.safetensors")).items():
            m = re.search(r"layers\.(\d+)\.(\w+\.\w+)\.lora_([AB])", k)
            if m:
                pairs.setdefault((int(m[1]), m[2]), {})[m[3]] = t
        alpha = float(cfg["lora_alpha"])
    else:  # MLX: lora_a [in,r], lora_b [r,out]; y += scale * x@a@b
        for k, t in load_file(os.path.join(path, "adapters.safetensors")).items():
            m = re.search(r"layers\.(\d+)\.(\w+\.\w+)\.lora_([ab])", k)
            if m:
                pairs.setdefault((int(m[1]), m[2]), {})[m[3].upper()] = t.T
        p = cfg["lora_parameters"]
        alpha = float(p["scale"]) * p["rank"]  # llama.cpp applies alpha/rank
    return {k: (v["A"], v["B"]) for k, v in pairs.items()}, alpha


def export(path):
    """Write <path>/adapter.gguf. -> its path."""
    import gguf, numpy as np
    pairs, alpha = _lora(path)
    if not pairs:
        sys.exit(f"no LoRA tensors in {path}")
    out = os.path.join(path, "adapter.gguf")
    w = gguf.GGUFWriter(out, "qwen2")
    w.add_type(gguf.GGUFType.ADAPTER)
    w.add_string(gguf.Keys.Adapter.TYPE, "lora")
    w.add_float32(gguf.Keys.Adapter.LORA_ALPHA, alpha)
    for (layer, proj), (a, b) in sorted(pairs.items()):
        if proj not in PROJ:
            sys.exit(f"can't map {proj} to GGUF")
        name = f"blk.{layer}.{PROJ[proj]}.weight"
        w.add_tensor(name + ".lora_a", np.ascontiguousarray(a, dtype=np.float32))
        w.add_tensor(name + ".lora_b", np.ascontiguousarray(b, dtype=np.float32))
    w.write_header_to_file(); w.write_kv_data_to_file(); w.write_tensors_to_file(); w.close()
    return out


def _up():
    try:
        urllib.request.urlopen(URL + "/api/version", timeout=3)
        return True
    except OSError:
        return False


def build():
    """(Re)create Ollama model `footprint` from the active adapter. Base model alone if none yet."""
    if not shutil.which("ollama"):
        sys.exit("Ollama not found. install: https://ollama.com/download  (mac: brew install ollama)")
    if not _up():
        sys.exit(f"Ollama not running at {URL}. start the Ollama app, or: ollama serve")
    b = base()
    subprocess.run(["ollama", "pull", b], check=True)
    lines = [f"FROM {b}"]
    if config.has_adapter():
        lines.append(f"ADAPTER {export(config.ADAPTERS)}")
        what = f"adapter {config.active_version()}"
    else:
        what = "no adapter yet (base model; run train)"
    mf = os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, "Modelfile")
    os.makedirs(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, exist_ok=True)
    open(mf, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    subprocess.run(["ollama", "create", NAME, "-f", mf], check=True)
    print(f"ollama model '{NAME}' = {b} + {what}\nOpenAI-compatible API: {URL}/v1  (model name: {NAME})")


if __name__ == "__main__":  # self-check: MLX and PEFT adapters both export to the same GGUF tensors
    import tempfile, numpy as np
    from safetensors.numpy import save_file
    import gguf
    a, b = np.random.rand(1536, 8).astype(np.float32), np.random.rand(8, 256).astype(np.float32)
    mlx, peft = tempfile.mkdtemp(), tempfile.mkdtemp()
    save_file({"model.layers.3.self_attn.k_proj.lora_a": a, "model.layers.3.self_attn.k_proj.lora_b": b},
              os.path.join(mlx, "adapters.safetensors"))
    json.dump({"lora_parameters": {"rank": 8, "scale": 2.0}}, open(os.path.join(mlx, "adapter_config.json"), "w"))
    save_file({"base_model.model.model.layers.3.self_attn.k_proj.lora_A.weight": a.T.copy(),
               "base_model.model.model.layers.3.self_attn.k_proj.lora_B.weight": b.T.copy()},
              os.path.join(peft, "adapter_model.safetensors"))
    json.dump({"lora_alpha": 16}, open(os.path.join(peft, "adapter_config.json"), "w"))
    got = []
    for d in (mlx, peft):
        r = gguf.GGUFReader(export(d))
        t = {x.name: x for x in r.tensors}
        assert set(t) == {"blk.3.attn_k.weight.lora_a", "blk.3.attn_k.weight.lora_b"}, set(t)
        assert list(t["blk.3.attn_k.weight.lora_a"].shape) == [1536, 8]  # ggml ne: [in, r]
        assert list(t["blk.3.attn_k.weight.lora_b"].shape) == [8, 256]   # ggml ne: [r, out]
        assert r.fields[gguf.Keys.Adapter.LORA_ALPHA].parts[-1][0] == 16.0
        got.append(np.array(t["blk.3.attn_k.weight.lora_a"].data))
    assert np.allclose(got[0], got[1])
    os.environ["FOOTPRINT_OLLAMA_BASE"] = ""
    config.MODEL = "mlx-community/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct-4bit"; assert base() == "qwen2.5-coder:7b"
    print("ok")

"""footprint — learn a local SLM from your Claude Code transcripts.

Commands:
  setup                 create .venv + install the platform backend (mlx / torch)
  trace                 arm tracing: sessions from now on become training data (run before chatting)
  collect [project|--all]  curated training data: accepted turns + your own commits, redacted, split by session (default: this project)
  train                 LoRA v2 on data/ -> new adapter version (live only if test loss improves)
  eval                  test loss + perplexity of the footprint adapter on held-out data
  adapter [use vN]      list adapter versions (* = live) with losses; use vN = switch / roll back
  serve                 OpenAI-compatible API at localhost:8399 (install runs this for you)
  install               auto-start server (launchd / systemd / Task Scheduler) + OpenCode /footprint
  context [install]     previous Claude session's state for this project; install = SessionStart hook
  bench [harvest|run|upload]  Claude-parity benchmark on your own tasks (any model)
  recall [text|--embed] similar past tasks from all your sessions (hook: added to each prompt); --embed = index all for semantic search
  profile               what new sessions learn about you + this project (also part of `context`)
  recall [text]         similar past tasks from all your sessions (hook: added to each prompt)
  memory list|forget|review|eval  what sessions are told about you (list [--all]); forget <id> drops a wrong
                        preference; review = mark each right/wrong; eval = correction rate, git outcomes, precision
  facts [--all]         structured memory: your stated preferences as JSON (hook: added at session start)
  switch [list|session] open latest (or chosen) Claude Code chat in OpenCode, full history; list = show ids
  status                what's collected/trained
  login [fp_key]        sign in with your website API key (no key = GitHub device flow)
  key list|revoke       list/revoke API keys (generate them on the website)
  sync push|pull [--with-data]  sync adapters/ (and, only if asked, training data/) via your vault
"""
import os, sys

from . import adapters, bench, config, context, memory, service, switch, transcripts, vault
from .backends import get


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    cmd = argv[0] if argv else "status"
    if cmd == "train" and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(config.DATA, "train.jsonl")):
        sys.exit("no data. run: footprint collect")
    {"collect": lambda: transcripts.collect(argv[1] if len(argv) > 1 else None),
     "trace": service.trace,
     "train": lambda: get().train(),
     "eval": lambda: get().evaluate(),
     "adapter": lambda: adapters.main(argv[1:]),
     "serve": lambda: get().serve(),
     "install": service.install,
     "context": lambda: context.show(argv[1:]),
     "switch": lambda: switch.switch(argv[1:]),
     "recall": lambda: memory.recall(argv[1:]),
     "profile": lambda: print(memory.profile(memory.build(), os.getcwd()) or "nothing learned yet"),
     "facts": lambda: memory.facts_cmd(argv[1:]),
     "memory": lambda: memory.memory_cmd(argv[1:]),
     "bench": lambda: bench.main(argv[1:]),
     "status": service.status,
     "setup": service.setup,
     "login": lambda: vault.login(argv[1:]),
     "key": lambda: vault.keys_cmd(argv[1:]),
     "sync": lambda: vault.sync_cmd(argv[1:])}.get(cmd, lambda: sys.exit(__doc__))()
#!/usr/bin/env node
const { spawnSync } = require("child_process");
const path = require("path");
const fs = require("fs");

const root = path.join(__dirname, "..");
const script = path.join(root, "footprint.py");
const win = process.platform === "win32";
const venvPy = win
  ? path.join(root, ".venv", "Scripts", "python.exe")
  : path.join(root, ".venv", "bin", "python");
const args = process.argv.slice(2);

if (args.length === 0) {
  require("./banner");
}

// context/collect/status are stdlib-only: system python, no venv, no model download.
// Only the local-model commands need the venv + backend (setup = local mode opt-in).
const sysPy = win ? "python" : "python3";
const needsModel = ["train", "eval", "serve", "install"].includes(args[0]);
if (needsModel && !fs.existsSync(venvPy)) {
  console.log("local model mode — setting up (venv + model backend, one-time)…");
  const s = spawnSync(sysPy, [script, "setup"], { stdio: "inherit" });
  if (s.status) process.exit(s.status);
}

const py = fs.existsSync(venvPy) ? venvPy : sysPy;
const r = spawnSync(py, [script, ...(args.length ? args : ["status"])], {
  stdio: "inherit",
});
process.exit(r.status === null ? 1 : r.status);

content.content:
## Requirements

| | trace / collect | train / serve |
|---|---|---|
| **macOS (Apple Silicon)** | ✅ | ✅ MLX backend |
| **Linux** | ✅ | ✅ torch backend (CUDA or CPU) |
| **Windows** | ✅ | ✅ torch backend (CUDA or CPU) |
| **macOS (Intel)** | ✅ | ✅ torch backend (CPU) |

- [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) installed and used at least once
- Python 3.9+
- Node.js 18+ (only if installing via npm)

footprint picks the backend automatically: [MLX](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx)
on Apple Silicon, PyTorch + PEFT everywhere else (uses CUDA when available;
CPU works but trains slowly — prefer a GPU or drop `FOOTPRINT_ITERS`).

## Install

### macOS

```sh
npm install -g footprint-trace
```

or from source:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Amanlabh/footprint.git
cd footprint

"""Serve through Ollama: LoRA adapter -> GGUF adapter -> `ollama create footprint` on Ollama's own base.

  adapters/<model>/vN/adapters.safetensors (MLX)  or  adapter_model.safetensors (PEFT, torch backend)
    -> vN/adapter.gguf  (a few MB; llama.cpp LoRA format)
    -> Modelfile: FROM <ollama base>  ADAPTER vN/adapter.gguf
    -> model "footprint" at http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1  (Ollama runs itself: app / brew service / systemd)
"""
import json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, urllib.request

from . import config

URL = os.environ.get("OLLAMA_HOST", "http://127.0.0.1:11434").rstrip("/")
if "://" not in URL:
    URL = "http://" + URL
NAME = "footprint"
# HF layer names -> llama.cpp/GGUF names (Qwen2 / Llama-style blocks)
PROJ = {"self_attn.q_proj": "attn_q", "self_attn.k_proj": "attn_k", "self_attn.v_proj": "attn_v",
        "self_attn.o_proj": "attn_output", "mlp.gate_proj": "ffn_gate", "mlp.up_proj": "ffn_up",
        "mlp.down_proj": "ffn_down"}


def base():
    """Ollama tag of the same base model footprint trained on."""
    if os.environ.get("FOOTPRINT_OLLAMA_BASE"):
        return os.environ["FOOTPRINT_OLLAMA_BASE"]
    m = re.search(r"Qwen2\.5-Coder-([\d.]+)B", config.MODEL, re.I)
    if not m:
        sys.exit(f"no Ollama base known for {config.MODEL}. set FOOTPRINT_OLLAMA_BASE (e.g. qwen2.5-coder:7b)")
    return f"qwen2.5-coder:{m.group(1)}b"


def _lora(path):
    """-> ({(layer, proj): (A[r,in], B[out,r])}, alpha) from an MLX or PEFT adapter dir."""
    from safetensors.numpy import load_file
    cfg = json.load(open(os.path.join(path, "adapter_config.json"), encoding="utf-8"))
    pairs = {}
    if os.path.exists(os.path.join(path, "adapter_model.safetensors")):  # PEFT: lora_A.weight [r,in], lora_B.weight [out,r]
        for k, t in load_file(os.path.join(path, "adapter_model.safetensors")).items():
            m = re.search(r"layers\.(\d+)\.(\w+\.\w+)\.lora_([AB])", k)
            if m:
                pairs.setdefault((int(m[1]), m[2]), {})[m[3]] = t
        alpha = float(cfg["lora_alpha"])
    else:  # MLX: lora_a [in,r], lora_b [r,out]; y += scale * x@a@b
        for k, t in load_file(os.path.join(path, "adapters.safetensors")).items():
            m = re.search(r"layers\.(\d+)\.(\w+\.\w+)\.lora_([ab])", k)
            if m:
                pairs.setdefault((int(m[1]), m[2]), {})[m[3].upper()] = t.T
        p = cfg["lora_parameters"]
        alpha = float(p["scale"]) * p["rank"]  # llama.cpp applies alpha/rank
    return {k: (v["A"], v["B"]) for k, v in pairs.items()}, alpha


def export(path):
    """Write <path>/adapter.gguf. -> its path."""
    import gguf, numpy as np
    pairs, alpha = _lora(path)
    if not pairs:
        sys.exit(f"no LoRA tensors in {path}")
    out = os.path.join(path, "adapter.gguf")
    w = gguf.GGUFWriter(out, "qwen2")
    w.add_type(gguf.GGUFType.ADAPTER)
    w.add_string(gguf.Keys.Adapter.TYPE, "lora")
    w.add_float32(gguf.Keys.Adapter.LORA_ALPHA, alpha)
    for (layer, proj), (a, b) in sorted(pairs.items()):
        if proj not in PROJ:
            sys.exit(f"can't map {proj} to GGUF")
        name = f"blk.{layer}.{PROJ[proj]}.weight"
        w.add_tensor(name + ".lora_a", np.ascontiguousarray(a, dtype=np.float32))
        w.add_tensor(name + ".lora_b", np.ascontiguousarray(b, dtype=np.float32))
    w.write_header_to_file(); w.write_kv_data_to_file(); w.write_tensors_to_file(); w.close()
    return out


def up():
    try:
        urllib.request.urlopen(URL + "/api/version", timeout=3)
        return True
    except OSError:
        return False


def build():
    """(Re)create Ollama model `footprint` from the active adapter. Base model alone if none yet."""
    if not shutil.which("ollama"):
        sys.exit("Ollama not found. install: https://ollama.com/download  (mac: brew install ollama)")
    if not up():
        sys.exit(f"Ollama not running at {URL}. start the Ollama app, or: ollama serve")
    b = base()
    subprocess.run(["ollama", "pull", b], check=True)
    lines = [f"FROM {b}"]
    v = config.active_version()  # not config.ADAPTERS: that is fixed at import, stale after `adapter use`
    path = os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, v or "none")
    if any(os.path.exists(os.path.join(path, f)) for f in ("adapters.safetensors", "adapter_model.safetensors")):
        lines.append(f"ADAPTER {export(path)}")
        what = f"adapter {v}"
    else:
        what = "no adapter yet (base model; run train)"
    mf = os.path.join(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, "Modelfile")
    os.makedirs(config.MODEL_ADAPTERS, exist_ok=True)
    open(mf, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    subprocess.run(["ollama", "create", NAME, "-f", mf], check=True)
    print(f"ollama model '{NAME}' = {b} + {what}\nOpenAI-compatible API: {URL}/v1  (model name: {NAME})")


def refresh():
    """After the live adapter changes: rebuild `footprint` if Ollama is there, else say how."""
    if shutil.which("ollama") and up():
        build()
    else:
        print("Ollama not running: start it, then `footprint install` to serve the new adapter")


if __name__ == "__main__":  # self-check: MLX and PEFT adapters both export to the same GGUF tensors
    import tempfile, numpy as np
    from safetensors.numpy import save_file
    import gguf
    a, b = np.random.rand(1536, 8).astype(np.float32), np.random.rand(8, 256).astype(np.float32)
    mlx, peft = tempfile.mkdtemp(), tempfile.mkdtemp()

    json.dump({"lora_parameters": {"rank": 8, "scale": 2.0}}, open(os.path.join(mlx, "adapter_config.json"), "w"))
    save_file({"base_model.model.model.layers.3.self_attn.k_proj.lora_A.weight": a.T.copy(),
               "base_model.model.model.layers.3.self_attn.k_proj.lora_B.weight": b.T.copy()},
              os.path.join(peft, "adapter_model.safetensors"))
    json.dump({"lora_alpha": 16}, open(os.path.join(peft, "adapter_config.json"), "w"))

        assert list(t["blk.3.attn_k.weight.lora_b"].shape) == [8, 256]   # ggml ne: [r, out]
        assert r.fields[gguf.Keys.Adapter.LORA_ALPHA].parts[-1][0] == 16.0
        got.append(np.array(t["blk.3.attn_k.weight.lora_a"].data))

content.text:
GGUF is a file format for storing a model's weights in one self-contained file. It comes from llama.cpp, the engine Ollama runs on.

**What's inside one file:**
- **The weights**, the model's numbers, usually compressed ("quantized"). For example Q4_K_M stores each weight in about 4.5 bits instead of 16, so the 1.5B model is about 1 GB instead of 3 GB.
- **Metadata**: architecture (`qwen2`), layer count, context length, the tokenizer and the chat template. You don't need any extra config files beside it.
- It's built to load fast: the file is mapped straight into memory, with no conversion step.

**Why footprint needs it:** Ollama only reads GGUF. MLX and PyTorch save LoRA adapters as `.safetensors` in their own layouts. So `ollama.py` converts:

```
adapters.safetensors (MLX)  →  adapter.gguf  (21 MB)
lora_a [in, r]                 blk.N.attn_q.weight.lora_a
lora_b [r, out]                blk.N.attn_q.weight.lora_b
scale × rank                   adapter.lora.alpha
```

Ollama then puts `qwen2.5-coder:1.5b`, which is already a GGUF file, and your adapter GGUF together at load time.

**How it compares to the other formats:**

| Format | Used by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| safetensors | Hugging Face, PyTorch, MLX | weights only; config and tokenizer are separate files |
| GGUF | llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio | one file with everything; many quantization levels |
| MLX 4-bit | Apple MLX | Mac only, fast on the Apple GPU |

The `gguf` Python package that `setup` now installs is the library llama.cpp publishes for reading and writing these files.

The biggest difference: the old Mac server most likely wasn't using your training at all. Here's how the two compare.

| | Before (mlx_lm server / torch server) | Now (Ollama) |
|---|---|---|
| **Your LoRA applied** | ❌ on Mac: mlx_lm 0.31.3 dropped the adapter, so the base model answered | ✅ checked: answers change to v1's style |
| **Model name `footprint`** | ❌ on Mac: mlx_lm treated it as a Hugging Face repo, so requests failed | ✅ Ollama serves it under that name |
| **Streaming** | torch: the whole answer arrived as one chunk at the end | ✅ token by token |
| **CPU on Linux/Windows without a GPU** | full-precision torch: slow, busy cores | 4-bit llama.cpp: several times faster (expected, not measured) |
| **Idle RAM** | model held in memory all the time (about 1–2 GB) | unloaded after 5 idle minutes |
| **Background service** | our own launchd/systemd/Task Scheduler setup, plus a log file in `/tmp` | Ollama manages itself; that code is gone |

**What got worse:**
- **One more thing to install**: Ollama itself.
- **Output isn't identical to training.** The adapter was trained on MLX's 4-bit model but runs on Ollama's Q4_K_M base. The style carries over, but the output isn't exactly the same as what the test loss measured.
- **The first request after 5 idle minutes is slower**, a few seconds while the model loads again.
- **On a Mac, speed is about the same.** Both run on the GPU, so don't expect a speedup there.

In short, on Mac it now works where it was broken before. On Linux and Windows it should also be faster and lighter, but I haven't measured that.

content.text:
After the first turn, follow-up turns in an OpenCode session now take about 1 s instead of 12 s or more. The catch: the first turn of a session still takes about 55 s.

Before this change, OpenCode was effectively broken on footprint. Its first prompt is about 12k tokens (system prompt plus tools), but Ollama's default context is 4096 tokens. So every request lost most of the prompt, and since the cut-off prompt never matched Ollama's cache, every turn re-read everything.

Measured through `/v1` with a 12k-token chat on your Mac:

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Context | 4096, prompt cut off | 16384 on your Mac, 32768 with 16 GB+ RAM |
| 1st turn | ~12 s, with most of the prompt missing | 55 s, with the full prompt |
| Turns 2 and 3 | ~12 s each (full re-read) | 1.1 s and 0.8 s |
| Unloads after | 5 idle minutes | 30 minutes after your last message |

What changed:
- **`ollama.py`:** the Modelfile now sets `PARAMETER num_ctx`, sized by RAM. Override it with `FOOTPRINT_NUM_CTX`.
- **Preloading:** `install` and `serve` now load the model right away, so the first request doesn't wait for a load.
- **OpenCode plugin:** each message you send to the footprint model also tells Ollama to keep it loaded for 30 minutes (`FOOTPRINT_KEEP_ALIVE`). Ollama's `/v1` API ignores keep-alive, so this goes through a separate request. I confirmed a `/v1` request doesn't cut that 30 minutes short.
- I reinstalled the plugin. I didn't test the keep-alive request inside a real OpenCode session, only Ollama's behaviour directly.
- The README and GUIDE list the two new settings.

Two other things I found:
- **Your Mac has 8 GB of RAM, not 16, and the disk is 99% full**, so it is swapping. That's why reading a prompt only runs at about 220 tokens/s, and why the first turn takes 55 s. Freeing disk space should help.
- **After roughly 16k tokens of conversation, the prompt gets cut off again** on your machine and every turn goes back to re-reading. That's the limit of 8 GB RAM.

Two ways to make the first turn faster, both needing your OK because they change Ollama's own settings for every model, not just footprint:
1. **Flash attention for Ollama:** `launchctl setenv OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION 1` and restart Ollama. Prompt reading on Apple GPUs is usually faster, but I haven't measured it here.
2. **Smaller attention cache:** `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`, which needs option 1. It halves that cache's memory, so 32k context would fit on 8 GB.

Nothing is committed yet. Should I commit and push to main, and try option 1 first?

  a keep_alive set through /api.

Measured via /v1 on an 8 GB M2, 12k-token chat: turn 1 55 s (full
prompt), turns 2-3 1.1 s / 0.8 s (was ~12 s each, truncated).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <[redacted]>
EOF

content.text:
Madhav's PR #9 (merged 2026-11-12) added `ram_gb()` in `footprint_core/config.py:212`. It reads the total RAM straight from the OS:

```python
def ram_gb():
    if IS_MAC:
        return int(subprocess.run(["sysctl", "-n", "hw.memsize"], ...).stdout) / 1e9
    return os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE") * os.sysconf("SC_PHYS_PAGES") / 1e9   # Linux
    # error -> None
```

- **Mac:** `sysctl hw.memsize` gives the size in bytes. Your Mac reports 8 589 934 592 bytes, which `ram_gb()` returns as **8.59**. That's 8 GiB, shown in decimal GB.
- **Linux:** page size × number of pages.
- **Windows:** `os.sysconf` doesn't exist there, so it returns `None` and the callers fall back to defaults.

There's no "8 GB" check anywhere. The number feeds three things:

1. **`seq_cap()`: the longest lesson it can train on without swapping.**
   - Formula: `(0.55 × RAM − weights) / (vocab × 4 bytes × 3 copies)`, rounded down to a multiple of 256, limited to the range `SEQ_MIN`–4096.
   - On your Mac: (0.55 × 8.59 − 0.9) / 0.00182 ≈ 2097, so **2048 tokens**. A 16 GB Mac gets the 4096 maximum.
   - Why: an 8 GB M1 at 4096 tokens swapped and did 0 steps in 8 minutes.

2. **`grad_ckpt()`: memory-saving mode while training (gradient checkpointing).** It turns on when the estimated peak memory from `train_mem_gb()` is more than half the RAM. If training still crashes from lack of memory, it turns on and resumes.
3. **My Ollama change uses the same `ram_gb()`.** Context is 32768 at 15 GB or more, otherwise 16384, so your Mac got 16384.

Settings to override it:
- `FOOTPRINT_MAX_SEQ` forces a lesson length.
- `FOOTPRINT_RAM_SHARE` sets how much of the RAM training may use (default 0.55).
- `FOOTPRINT_GRAD_CKPT` takes `on` or `off`.

Your last training run did use 8 GB settings, not 16. Here's what the v2 run saved (`progress.json`, `adapter_config.json`):

| Setting | Your run | Your Mac (8.59 GB) | A 16 GB Mac |
|---|---|---|---|
| Max lesson length (`seq`) | **2048** | 2048 | 4096 |
| Memory-saving mode (`grad_checkpoint`) | **on** | on | off when it fits |
| Lessons per validation check | 12 | 12 | 12 |

Running it now gives `ram 8.59 → seq_cap 2048, grad_ckpt True`. The README's "8 GB → 1792" is the self-check's number for exactly 8.0 GB. Your Mac reports 8.59 GB, which rounds to 2048.

Here's where "16 GB" shows up, which may be what you saw:
- **My mistake:** my commit `3bb8b73` says "Checked on a 16 GB M2". It was your 8 GB machine. Commit messages can't be fixed without rewriting history on main, so I've left it.
- **Madhav's numbers:** his commit and the code comments in `config.py` (lines 52, 169, 225) say "16 GB M2". That's his machine, where he calibrated the formulas.
- **The 7B tip** in the README is for Macs with 16 GB or more.

The real problem with that run is `"done": 0`: it stopped before finishing the first step. The likeliest reason is disk space. Your disk had about 1 GB free, and macOS needs free disk to grow swap. With VS Code, Claude and Ollama open, a 2048-token run (which can use up to about 4.7 GB) probably filled RAM and couldn't swap, so it stalled.

What did you see that said 16 GB: a printed line in the terminal, or something else? Paste it and I'll trace it. Otherwise, the fix is to free about 10 GB of disk and re-run. You can also force shorter lessons with `FOOTPRINT_MAX_SEQ=1536`.

lastPrompt: okay so after madhav push will now be training time be reduced ?

content.text:
Yes, training should take roughly half as long on your data, and it no longer keeps growing as you collect more sessions.

| | Before Madhav's changes | After (PR #8, #9, #10) |
|---|---|---|
| Steps | lessons × 2 (397 lessons → 794 steps) | 1 pass over the picked lessons, at most 300 (`FOOTPRINT_STEP_BUDGET`) |
| Growth with more sessions | kept growing | stops at 300 steps |
| Stopping | always ran every step | stops when validation loss hasn't improved for 2 checks (`FOOTPRINT_PATIENCE`) |
| Each validation check | 25 lessons (~70 s) | 12 lessons |
| Lessons on 8 GB | up to 4096 tokens, so it swapped (0 steps in 8 min) | capped at 2048, no swapping |
| Interrupted run | started over | resumes from its last checkpoint |
| Removed before training | — | low-quality lessons and near-copies |

**Madhav's measurement on his 16 GB Mac (83 lessons):**

| Run | Time | Test loss |
|---|---|---|
| Picked 40 lessons | 10 min | 2.467 |
| All 83 lessons | 26.5 min | 2.447 |

About 2.6× faster for nearly the same test loss. The run that picked 40 must have used a smaller step budget than the default.

**What this means for you (33 lessons):**
- 300 is more than 33, so selection keeps all of them except low-quality lessons and near-copies.
- So you go from 66 steps to 33 or fewer, about 2× faster, plus whatever early stopping saves.
- **New one-time cost:** before the first run, the untrained model scores every lesson (the "surprise" ranking). That adds a few minutes, and it's cached in `data/scores.json` after that.
- Your 8 GB Mac is slower per step than Madhav's 16 GB one, so expect more than 10 minutes.

**One thing still stops it:** your disk. The last run stalled at 0 steps, very likely because macOS couldn't grow swap with about 1–3 GB free. Free about 10 GB, then run `footprint train` and it will start the v2 run from the beginning (it saved no checkpoint). Want me to start it once you have the space?

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- When you fan work out in parallel, give each independent lookup `effort: "lower"` — that is where the step cheaper pays most. More generally, pass `"lower"` for any mechanical, self-checking brief (find-and-report, grep across named files, a pattern you spelled out); pass `"higher"` for a well-specified piece that needs more reasoning than the work around it.
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. "lower" or "higher" is one step from the effort the agent would otherwise run at (normally yours), on whatever model it would otherwise use. Pass "lower" when the brief is mechanical and checkable against itself — bounded search, grep-and-report, a pattern you spelled out. Pass "higher" when one well-specified piece needs more reasoning than the work around it. Omit when neither clearly applies.
